sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Auburn Hills, Michigan?
sections.html:
Auburn Hills is an Oakland County business hub with a young, renter-heavy population, so many local houses sell to buyers who work for the area's auto and tech employers. The Census Bureau counts 25,925 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 6.4 percent from the 2020 base, and only 51.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

The city sits about 26 miles north of downtown Detroit and covers 16.60 square miles of land. The median age in the 2020 census was 31.7, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $245,000 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. The city also has a lot of single-person households: persons per household average 2.10.

Selling here comes down to listing it, selling it directly or taking a cash offer. Whichever you pick, the local steps are the same: city rental or vacancy registration where it applies, the deed recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and the new-owner filing with the city assessor.

sections.h2: How did Auburn Hills become a city?
sections.html:
Auburn Hills was formed in 1983 when Pontiac Township merged with the village of Auburn Heights. The township began in 1821 as Pontiac Township, and a settler built a sawmill and grist mill on the Clinton River, which drew the first residents to the village of Auburn.

The village was renamed Amy in 1880 and became Auburn Heights in 1919. An earlier attempt to incorporate as Pontiac Heights in 1971 was denied by state officials, and the township became a charter township in 1978 to protect itself from annexation before the 1983 merger. The name Auburn Hills first appeared in 1964, when Oakland Community College named its campus for the area.

That history explains the layout. The old village center sits at Auburn and Squirrel roads, which the city redeveloped in 2002 as the Village Center, and the rest of the city grew in a pattern of business parks and subdivisions along I-75.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Auburn Hills and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Auburn Hills has facilities of more than 50 automotive companies and about 80,000 people working in its tech and office buildings during the day, which supports steady demand for nearby rentals and starter homes. Stellantis has its North American headquarters in the city, and the area also hosts BorgWarner, PHINIA, Guardian Industries, Autoliv, Joyson Safety Systems, GKN Driveline, Faurecia and Volkswagen and Audi's North American headquarters.

  • Oakland University has its main campus in Auburn Hills, and Oakland Community College has a campus here.
  • Great Lakes Crossing Outlets opened on November 12, 1998.
  • The Oakland Technology Park was approved in 1985.
  • The Palace of Auburn Hills, the former home of the Detroit Pistons, has been demolished.

Three school districts serve the city: Avondale School District, Pontiac School District and Rochester Community Schools. Avondale operates two elementary schools inside the city limits, Graham and Auburn, and all Avondale residents attend Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. In 2020 to 2024, 69.9 percent of residents aged 16 and older were in the labor force, and the mean commute was 22.1 minutes.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Auburn Hills housing?
sections.html:
The numbers show a mid-priced market with a large renter base and high education levels. The table below lists the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates for the city.

With a median rent of $1,477 against a median owner cost with a mortgage of $1,570, renting and owning cost similar amounts per month, which keeps buyers who plan to live in the home in the mix alongside investors.

sections.h2: Does Auburn Hills regulate rental and vacant homes?
sections.html:
Yes. Any detached one-family home that is rented or offered for rent must be registered with the city's Community Development Department, and a house that sits vacant must be registered too. A buyer who plans to rent a house you sell will meet these rules.

  • Registration costs $200, the permit to occupy $50, and the annual renewal $250, due December 31 each year.
  • An owner can ask the city to inspect the interior for $155, or file a self-certification checklist instead.
  • Failing to register carries a $100 first penalty plus possible civil infraction tickets.
  • A new owner of an existing rental must register again and get a new permit within 30 days after the sale.
  • A vacant home must be registered within 30 days of becoming vacant, and the registration form lists a $355 fee.

A letter from the city asking you to register does not always mean you are renting, because the city flags homes that are not claimed as a homestead. If you receive one, return a Statement of Exemption for a non-rental home and no fee applies. The Community Development Department is at 1827 N. Squirrel Road and answers at 248-364-6900.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded for Auburn Hills sales in Oakland County?
sections.html:
The Oakland County Register of Deeds records the deed, and warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed containing a warranty clause must first be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office. The Register of Deeds can be reached at 248-858-0597 and is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The state transfer tax is $3.75 per $500 and the county tax is 55 cents per $500, which comes to $8.60 per $1,000. On a $245,000 sale, the median value here, that is $2,107, owed by the seller. The deed must show the total value of the property or carry an affidavit that states it. Ask the Register of Deeds for the current recording fee, since the state default of $30 per document can differ in a charter county.

The county takes electronic recording through approved vendors. Its MiPropDocs service is limited to documents that do not transfer ownership, so a deed goes through a vendor, in person or by mail.

sections.h2: What must a seller and buyer file with the Auburn Hills assessor?
sections.html:
The buyer must file a Property Transfer Affidavit with the city assessor within 45 days of the sale, and a late residential filing costs $5 per day up to a $200 maximum. The assessor's office is open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Michigan property tax starts from the status of the property on tax day, December 31 of the year before. Assessed value is half of true cash value, and taxable value is the lesser of the state equalized value and the capped value. The cap rises each year by inflation or 5 percent, whichever is lower, unless ownership transfers.

  • You rescind your principal residence exemption on the old home with Form 2602, ideally at closing and in any case within 90 days of moving out.
  • A buyer who moves in before the May 1 filing deadline can claim the exemption on the new home with Form 2368.
  • A buyer who moves in between June 2 and November 1 can claim it for winter taxes only that year.

Closing agents are expected to supply the forms at the closing table, but the law gives no remedy against an agent who forgets, so check that both are on the list before you sign.

faqs.q: Does Auburn Hills require an inspection before I sell my house?
faqs.a: The city's pages do not list a sales inspection. Rental homes and vacant homes do have registration rules, so ask Community Development at 248-364-6900 whether your property falls into either group.

faqs.q: How much is the Michigan transfer tax on an Auburn Hills sale?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000, with $3.75 per $500 to the state and 55 cents per $500 to the county. The seller owes it, so a $245,000 sale costs $2,107.

faqs.q: What happens to a rental registration when I sell an Auburn Hills rental house?
faqs.a: The new owner must register again and obtain a new permit to occupy within 30 days after the sale. The new owner pays the $200 registration and $50 permit fees and files a self-certification checklist.

faqs.q: Which county handles deeds for Auburn Hills?
faqs.a: Oakland County. Its Register of Deeds records the deed, and the county treasurer tax certifies warranty deeds before recording.

faqs.q: How soon must the buyer file the transfer affidavit in Auburn Hills?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the transfer. A late residential filing carries a $5 per day penalty up to $200.
